cycles.name: Bedrock
focuses: Re-load two years of detrained tissue with tempo and isometric strength work.
Re-groove every movement pattern and armour the coaching wear zones.
Log week-one baselines on all three main lifts.

paragraphs: Four years training together, two years away, and you're back. That's what this month is really about. Bedrock is the base layer of everything we're going to build.

Your strength comes back fast, muscle memory is real and you have 4 years of it stored. Tendons are slower, they need time under load. So everything this month is slow and controlled on purpose. Three days a week, under an hour, built to fit around your court schedule.
By the end of week 4 you'll have your baseline numbers logged, joints that accept load again, and a clean base under you. Then we start collecting your strength back.
outcomes: Baseline numbers logged on all three main lifts
12 controlled sessions done around court weeks
Squat, hinge and single-leg patterns automatic again
Calf and elbow armour routines running

cycles.name: Strength Reclaim
focuses: Rebuild maximal strength on heavy bilateral lifts, intensity before volume.
Muscle returns through back-off volume while elastic groundwork begins.

paragraphs: Cycle 2 is called Strength Reclaim. The slow tempo work has done its job by then, and the bar finally starts climbing. Heavy, short sessions that fit your life exactly like this month does. Four years of strength is stored in your body and next month we go collect it.

cycles.name: Power Transfer
focuses: Convert rebuilt strength into rate of force development with jumps and throws.
Plyometric volume budgeted around court hours and play days.

cycles.name: Court Voltage
focuses: Express the new engine in tennis actions, serve power and first step.
Gym volume drops so freshness shows on playing days.

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.note: Two years off means we start lighter than your ego wants. Ramp up with 2 or 3 easy sets first, then week 1 stays at RPE 6. Your tendons need the head start, your strength will catch up fast.

cards.title: Week One: Find Your Numbers
cards.body:
The app never gives you a weight. You find it with the RPE target. Week 1 everything is RPE 6, which means you end every set knowing you had 4 more clean reps in you. Start lighter than you think. The first set will tell you if you should go up.

From week 2: hit all the reps at or under the target RPE, then add a little next time. Small jumps, one small plate at a time. Some weeks it will feel too easy. Good. That headroom is protecting your tendons while they catch up.

Some days last week's weight feels heavier. Drop it down. Going lighter on a rough day is the plan working. Nothing is lost.

And log every set this month. Cycle 2 gets built from those numbers.

cards.title: The First Month Trap
cards.body:
Here's the thing about coming back after 2 years. Strength returns in weeks, tendons take months. Around weeks 3 to 6 you'll feel strong and want to push. That exact moment is where comebacks go wrong.

Four spots to listen to: your Achilles, the front of your knee, high up the back of your thigh, and the outside of your elbow.

  • Normal: muscle burn during a set, tired legs, next day stiffness that fades by midday.
  • Not normal: a sharp spot, pain that builds through a set, or morning stiffness in one of those four places that is still there the next day.

If one shows up, message me before your next session. We pull that pattern back for a week and keep everything else moving. One quiet week beats a lost month.

cards.title: Court Days and Gym Days
cards.body:
Most of your gym days will also be court days. That's your life, and the program is built for it.

  • Lift after coaching, not before. Or leave 4 to 6 hours between them.
  • No gap possible? Run the short version: the day's main lift plus one pull, main lift kept easy.
  • Real match tomorrow? Don't do Day 1 or Day 3 today. Move it or run the short version. Legs stay fresh for match day, always.
  • The app asks how you feel before each session. Answer it honestly and it will tell you to take things one notch easier on rough days.

Days can move around your week. Just keep one day without lifting between Day 1 and Day 3.

cards.title: Your Sleep Is the Job
cards.body:
You rated your sleep 4 out of 10. You're in bed 7 to 8 hours, so the hours are fine. The quality is what's stealing your recovery, and this whole program runs on recovery.

  • Same sleep and wake time every day, even after late coaching.
  • Caffeine stops after lunch.
  • Screen off 30 minutes before bed. Room dark and cool.

Pick one this week, add the next one next week. We'll go through it at every check-in. Fix the sleep and everything in this program pays double.

cards.title: Eat Like You Train
cards.body:
You told me your eating has no structure right now. At 66 kg with muscle on the goal list, food is half this program.

  • Protein at every meal. A palm-sized portion minimum. Chicken, meat, fish, eggs, yogurt.
  • Don't train empty. Something real 2 to 3 hours before lifting, even on a coaching day.
  • Eat properly after sessions. That's when the rebuild happens.

No counting, no apps, not yet. Just these three rules for 4 weeks. We look at it together at the check-ins and build from there.

cards.title: Two Minutes for Your Elbow
cards.body:
You feed thousands of balls a week. That load lands on the outside of the elbow, and it's exactly how tennis elbow starts. We armour it before it ever complains.

On days you don't lift: light band or a small weight, palm down, lift the back of your hand up slow, lower it slower. 12 to 15 reps, 2 rounds each side. Two minutes, 2 to 3 times a week.

Do it in front of the TV. Boring on purpose. It works.
